# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_012_page_001.jpg

---

**12:1** For your imperishable Spirit is in all things.

**12:2** Therefore you correct those who err little by little, and you remind and warn them through the things in which they sin, so that they may be released from evil and believe in you, O Lord.

**12:3** For even the ancient inhabitants of your holy land you hated,

**12:4** because they practiced the most detestable works — sorcery and unholy rites,

**12:5** merciless slaughters of children, and sacrificial feasts of human flesh and blood conducted in the midst of initiatory rites,

**12:6** and parents who were murderers of helpless souls — these you were determined to destroy by the hands of our ancestors,

**12:7** so that the land most precious to you might receive a worthy settlement of the children of God.

**12:8** But even these you spared as human beings, and you sent hornets as harbingers of your army, to destroy them little by little.

**12:9** Not that you were unable to give over the ungodly into the hands of the righteous in battle, or to destroy them at once by terrible beasts or by your harsh word;

**12:10** but judging them gradually you gave them time and place for repentance, not being unaware that their lineage was evil and their wickedness inborn, and that their way of thinking would never change —

**12:11** for they were a cursed seed from the beginning — nor was it through fear of anyone that you left their sins unpunished.

**12:12** For who will say, "What have you done?" or who will oppose your judgment? And who will accuse you for having destroyed nations that you yourself made? Or who will come before you as an advocate for the unrighteous?

**12:13** For there is no god besides you who cares for all, to whom you would need to demonstrate that you have not judged unjustly;

**12:14** nor can any king or ruler stand before you in defense of those you have punished.

**12:15** Being righteous yourself, you govern all things righteously, judging it incompatible with your power to condemn one who does not deserve to be punished.

**12:16** For your strength is the source of righteousness, and your sovereignty over all makes you lenient toward all.

**12:17** For you demonstrate your strength when people disbelieve in the perfection of your power, and you rebuke any overstepping in those who are aware of it.

**12:18** But you, master of strength, judge with forbearance and govern us with great restraint, for the power is ready at hand whenever you choose to use it.

**12:19** Through such deeds you taught your people that the righteous man must be a friend of humanity, and you gave your children the good hope that you grant repentance for sins.

**12:20** For if with such great care and forbearance you punished the enemies of your children — men who deserved to die — giving them times and opportunity by which they might be released from their wickedness,

**12:21** with how great precision did you judge your own sons, to whose ancestors you gave oaths and covenants full of good promises!

**12:22** Therefore while disciplining us you scourge our enemies ten-thousandfold, so that when we judge we may reflect on your goodness, and when we are judged we may look for mercy.

**12:23** Hence also those who lived in folly and unrighteousness you tormented through their own abominations.

**12:24** For they had gone far astray on the paths of error, taking as gods the creatures most despised even among animals, and being deceived like foolish children.

**12:25** Therefore, as to unreasoning children, you sent a judgment that mocked them.

**12:26** But those who would not be corrected by a playful rebuke will experience a judgment worthy of God.

**12:27** For in the very things over which they suffered indignation, the things they thought to be gods — suffering punishment through those things — they finally saw and recognized the true God, whom before they had refused to know. And so the final condemnation came upon them.
